_readme: Every tunable value for the 'How do you test a conversation?' demo video.
This is the ONLY file to edit for a parameter change — never timing.json,
which is generated/projected and costs thousands of tokens to read.
Cost routing lives in .github/skills/demo-recording/SKILL.md. Only the
'audio' block is cheap to change; everything else forces a full re-render.
Continuity values are inherited from the two sibling videos under
three sit together if ever played back-to-back.

project.name: eval-loop-demo
project.title: How do you test a conversation?
project.lede: Hundreds of simulated customers, each with their own knowledge of their own problem, run against a pull-request branch before anyone opens the review.
project.objective: Viewer will be able to explain how we simulate hundreds of customers to evaluate a conversational AI change, and decide to ask for the same evidence on their own AI features.
project.audience: Engineering leadership / partner-level. Assume they know what an LLM and a pull request are. Assume nothing about the support interview.
project.callToAction: Run it against your branch before you open the pull request.
noGo: Environment or endpoint hostnames of any kind — say 'we deploy the pull-request branch and point the harness at it'
test1 / test2 / any deployment slot name
Azure DevOps pull-request numbers, in narration OR on screen
Verbatim text from the 50 golden-disambiguation scenarios — they derive from real customer queries; reference them, never quote them
'SAP path' as spoken jargon — say 'support category' or 'the exact category'
'L5' / 'L4' as spoken jargon — say 'the most specific level' / 'one level up'
project.series: interviewer-qna (loose — standalone, shares house style only)
project.seriesNote: Standalone. Voice/speed/gap/loudness match interviewer-qna-delta so the three can be shown together. Music preset deliberately differs.
project._preTrainingNote: Assumes nothing. Segment 1 establishes what the interview is and what 'getting it right' means before any harness detail.

accessibility._note: Planning-time constraints. See references/planning.md §3 and the plan's §2.E.
accessibility._narrationNote: Audited at authoring time. Every on-screen figure is spoken with its unit and denominator; every diagram state change is narrated as a transition. No bare 'this' or 'here'. Re-audit if any segment's visual changes.
accessibility._colorNote: Refusal polarity, grades and the regressed-probe row all carry a text label, never colour alone. The two-tier comparison uses labelled lanes, not two colours.
accessibility._contrastNote: PENDING — measure at draft render. All text is rendered natively by write-build-html rather than cropped from the report HTML, specifically so contrast is controlled rather than inherited from a 'color-scheme: light dark' page.
accessibility._flashingNote: PENDING — verify at draft render. Segment 4 is the only real risk and is deliberately a FILLING progress bar, not a strobing grid. Cap 3 state changes/sec (WCAG 2.3.1).
accessibility.captionPlan: Verbatim from script.md after the locked render.

pronunciations.UI: you eye — but prefer the word 'interface' in narration

narration.numbersConvention: Spelled out in narration, with unit and — on first use — denominator. Replicate counts as 'three runs', never '3x'. Ratios as 'point'. Every figure that appears on screen is also spoken (WCAG G226).
narration._numbersNote: The report's means carry one decimal (21.3, 11.7, 17.7). Speak the decimal rather than rounding, so narration and the on-screen row agree exactly.

downstream.reuse: Likely one or two slides. Not a documentation source — per Diátaxis a walkthrough is not a lossless reference.

gateDecisions._note: Answered by the approver at the SKILL.md §4 gate. Recorded so a later session does not re-ask (references/planning.md §1).

q1_bddComparisonWeight.question: How hard should segment 2 lean on the behaviour-suite comparison?
q1_bddComparisonWeight.answer: Keep as written — ~20s, complementary framing. Revisit later if it runs long.

q2_playgroundScreenCapture.question: May a 5-8s screen capture of the interface harness driving the real Playground be used?
q2_playgroundScreenCapture.answer: Yes. Redaction is a light pass — the scenarios are authored test data and carry no personal information.
q2_playgroundScreenCapture.effect: Segment 6 SPLIT into `twotier` + `blindspot`, because write-build-html resolves `footage` per segment rather than as a mid-segment overlay. 7 segments became 8. The clip is NOT yet captured; `blindspot` degrades to its stage-trace diagram until one is registered approvedForUse + redaction:'clear' in evidence-pack/footage/clips.json.
q2_playgroundScreenCapture.residualCheck: Account chrome and any hostname must still be off-screen — the harness drives a named host.

output._resolutionNote: Raised from 1920x1080 to 3840x2160, aspect unchanged at 16:9, so the 0 0 1600 520 diagram viewBoxes remain valid — only pixel dimensions change. write-build-html MUST be re-run after any change here or frame-capture throws 'stage/viewport mismatch'.
output._frameFormatNote: MEASURED, not assumed. At 3840x2160 with dedup off: PNG 1.00 fps and 2,183 KB/frame; JPEG q88 13.05 fps and 170 KB/frame — 13x faster, 12.8x smaller. Playwright's PNG screenshot losslessly compresses 8.3M pixels per frame, and that dominates capture cost at 4K. Quality checked at 1:1 on small type over flat backgrounds: crisp edges, no ringing or blocking. This makes 4K JPEG capture CHEAPER than the 1080p PNG render previously shipped.

voice.name: en-US-AndrewNeural
voice._speedNote: 1.2 matches what the sibling video ACTUALLY rendered (calibration-observed.json:roundedSpeed). Its intake-constraints.json says 1.1 — that value never reached a render. Use 1.2.

timing._wpsNote: 3.372 is the sibling video's MEASURED effective rate at 1.2x (calibration-observed.json). Its conservative counterpart, observedSafeWps 2.81, is the pessimistic bound. This script is number-dense, so the true rate likely sits between them — synthesis (S3, ~1 min) settles it before anything expensive runs.
timing._note: perceivedGap is what a viewer HEARS: tail(clip N) + inserted silence + head(clip N+1), not the length of the inserted file. See bug-ledger entry 6.

endCard._note: OFF, and it stays off. The canonical disabled form per timing-schema.json: builderVersion, contentMs and outroMs must all be ABSENT, and durationMs must equal the last segment's endMs. Do not add a tagline or builderVersion pad.
endCard._attributionInvariant: PROJECT INVARIANT: audio.music.attribution non-null => endCard.enabled MUST be true. The end card is the only credit surface this video has, so a later track swap to a licence that requires attribution cannot be made without also re-enabling the card. Enforced by tests/write-script.test.mjs.

audio._note: THE CHEAP BLOCK. Changes here swap the audio track and reuse the video stream byte-for-byte.

music.title: Corporate Ambient
music.creator: Kulakovka

loop._note: The track is 158.46s against a 250.63s video — 92.17s short. amix duration=longest does NOT extend a short input; it leaves the tail with no bed and says nothing (bug-ledger entry 15). remux-music.mjs now loops with a crossfade at each wrap and trims to length, and errors loudly under --no-loop.

music._presetNote: Only used when generated:true. The generated 'bright' bed was replaced by the licensed track above; the sibling interviewer-qna-delta used generated 'warm'.
music._licenceNote: Pixabay Content License requires no attribution and permits commercial use without credit. The creator credit was offered and declined, so no credit surface is needed — which is why endCard stays disabled. See the invariant below.

levels._musicGainNote: MEASURED, not inherited, and re-derived after a 24 dB drift. The licensed track is a commercial master at RMS -11.4 dB, so the gain is musicUnderSpeechDb minus that: -41 - -11.4 = -29.6 dB = 0.031 linear. VERIFIED by decoding three narration-free gaps: -42.1, -40.9, -41.7 dB. HOW IT DRIFTED: a review asked for "music 1.50 -> 0.85" believing the current value was 1.50; 1.50 was the GENERATED bed gain from the sibling project and this project had been on a file source for rounds. The absolute number was applied without re-deriving it and the bed shipped at -12.0 dB. ASK FOR A TARGET LEVEL, NOT A GAIN VALUE. "Put the bed at -41 dB" is checkable against the file; "set the gain to 0.85" carries a hidden assumption about what the gain currently is. Bug-ledger entry 16.
levels._duckingNote: A file bed CANNOT duck, so musicInGapsDb IS NOT HONOURED FOR FILE SOURCES. make-music.mjs bakes sidechain ducking in from vo-envelope.json; remux-music.mjs has no sidechaincompress path for a file input, so the track plays flat and ONE gain has to serve two targets 6 dB apart. Under-speech is the one chosen, so the gaps and the lead-in sit ~6 dB below where they should be. Do not tune musicInGapsDb expecting an effect on this project — it is a knob the code cannot currently honour. Engine feedback is filed: a file source should duck like a generated one, and this will recur for every project using a licensed track rather than the synth bed, which is now the expected path.
levels._note: Narration level MUST match interviewer-qna-delta — verify with check-levels.mjs against that file, not against the target.
levels._voiceGainNote: Raised 1.18 -> 1.40 at explicit user request ("lift the voice"). This DELIBERATELY breaks the narration-level match with interviewer-qna-delta. Do not "fix" it back without asking — the divergence is intentional and was requested after listening.
levels._targetNote: targetIntegratedDb -19.5 is an RMS figure from an earlier round and is NOT LUFS — the two are not comparable. Measured integrated loudness of the shipped mix is -14.4 LUFS at -1.8 dBTP. That is still hotter than a typical streaming target (~-16 LUFS), which is a consequence of the requested voice lift; the true-peak ceiling is met with room to spare.

fades._note: fades.inMs MUST stay shorter than timing.leadInMs (2000) or the bed arrives under the narration. Bug-ledger entry 4.

limiter._note: MUST stay false. ffmpeg alimiter defaults to level=true and gain-rides the whole mix. Bug-ledger entry 1.

render._note: 38 min is SCALED from the reference implementation's ~9-10x runtime, not measured on this machine. Replace both values from the first real run and record the per-stage split in render-log.md.
render._measureNote: No render has been run for this project. Nothing below S2 has executed.
